text:
anya: Quick walkthrough — I pushed a draft Grafana panel for prefix-cache hit-rate propagation. Preview link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/prefix-prop (panel set includes per-model / per-route / per-customer slices)

devon: Saw that. There's a visible hit-rate dip for neo-13B tenant-acme around the epoch earlier today. Token-saved metric drops by ~45% on that slice. Any deploys coincident?

matt: We rolled a kernel-selector tweak ~3409869000 that biases batching toward kernel v2.2 for medium-length sequences. Could affect how keys line up across batches.

samir: Did a quick profile: KV miss rate for model=neo-13B increased from ~2% -> ~7% after the selector change. Flamegraphs show more time spent in key lookup retries.

jun: Also noticed batching heuristic prefers larger micro-batches now, so sequence boundary alignment shifts. I added a small entropy plot to the panel showing increased prefix-key variance.

anya: On the dashboard I added a token-saved waterfall and a per-route breakdown. The biggest loss is from route=completion/plain-text (long prompts).

matt: Could be a key-normalization regression — we toggled strip-trailing-whitespace earlier for perf. @devon did that change touch keying?

devon: Yes — I changed normalize_prefix=true -> false in the fast-path to save CPU cycles. That reduces canonicalization but increases key cardinality. I can revert with a targeted micro-optimization.

perf-bot: Deploy 3409876120 -> kernel-selector v2.2 applied to region us-west-2 (status: success)

samir: Reverting normalization will add a small CPU delta. Need canary to measure latency p50/p99 impact vs token-saved gains. My recommendation: canary on low-traffic tenant + export detailed KV miss traces.

anya: Good call. Can we add a synthetic test in perf-harness that emulates long prefix distribution for neo-13B so we can reproduce locally?

matt: I'll add a workload that ramps long prompts and measures prefix_cache_hitrate, kv_miss_rate, median_p99_latency. Also add an alert: absolute hit-rate drop > 3% over 10m for any (model, route, customer) slice.

jun: Sharing the query snippets I used for the panel (Grafana/PromQL):

```promql
# per-customer prefix hit rate (5m)
sum(rate(prefix_cache_hit_total[5m])) by (customer, model, route) /
sum(rate(prefix_cache_lookup_total[5m])) by (customer, model, route)
```

```promql
# token-saved waterfall (approx)
sum(rate(prefix_cache_saved_tokens_total[5m])) by (customer, model, route)
```

devon: I'll open a PR to re-enable normalization on the key fast-path but keep the fast hash path for common cases. Will include microbench numbers. ETA: EOD.

anya: Action items: 1) @devon - PR for key normalization + micro-opts, canary instructions. 2) @matt - perf harness workload + alert. 3) @jun - add neo-13B tenant-acme slice and entropy chart to the shared dashboard. I'll create tracking tickets and link here.

devon: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4923 - includes benchmark table and toggles for canary.

samir: I'll instrument additional KV trace spans (lightweight) for the canary to get exact miss reasons.

matt: Alert rule pushed to staging. Panel id for the hit-rate explainer is 72; added short blurb: 'hit-rate can drift when kernel selection or batching heuristics change — keys may realign or become more granular.'

anya: Thanks team. We'll watch canary for 2 hours then reconvene if alerts fire. If token-saved doesn't recover, we'll rollback selector change. Meeting tentatively tomorrow 09:30 PT to review results. :thumbsup:
